title: Luntian 1 mungbean (NSIC Mg 19): Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaTitle: Luntian 1 mungbean: Yield, Maturity and Characteristics
metaDescription: Luntian 1 mungbean is a mungbean variety. About 60 days to harvest, 1.3 t/ha in trials. See its pest ratings and traits.
excerpt: Luntian 1 is a registered mungbean variety, also sold or known as NSIC Mg 19 or Luntian munggo. It was registered with the National Seed Industry Council in 2018 as NSIC 2018 Mg 19. It takes about 60 days from sowing to harvest, with 1.34 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials.

blocks.text: If you came here looking for NSIC Mg 19 or Luntian munggo, this is the same mungbean. Its seller and farm sources add notes, listed at the end. Compare it with the others in our [mungbean variety finder](/crop-varieties/mungbean), or see [every crop variety](/crop-varieties) we list. For the crop itself, read our guide: [Land preparation for legumes](/land-preparation/legume-land-preparation).

blocks.text: How long does it take, and how much does it yield?

Luntian 1 mungbean takes about 60 days from sowing to harvest. That is about the average of the 33 mungbean varieties with a day count, 59.8 days. A shorter crop frees the field sooner and dodges more of the weather, while a longer one often fills more.

Its average yield of 1.34 t/ha beats the average of its group, 1.25. It sits in the top quarter of its group. Trial yields come from well managed plots, so your own will depend on water, fertilizer, pests and timing. Its seller gives 60 to 61 days.

Once you know the day count, anee.io dates every task from each lot's own planting day, with [the growth stages and weather](/features/growth-stages-and-weather) beside it.
Is it resistant to pests and diseases?

blocks.caption: Reactions in trials, rated under natural field conditions

blocks.text: It showed no weak spot in the ratings on record. Still, a resistant variety can break down when a new strain or pest population comes, so keep scouting. Read up on [Cercospora leaf spot](/diseases/cercospora-leaf-spot).

The pests and diseases that hit mungbean fields most often: [bean fly](/pests/bean-fly), [legume pod borer](/pests/legume-pod-borer), [powdery mildew](/diseases/powdery-mildew), [thrips](/pests/thrips). Our [pest finder](/pests) and [disease finder](/diseases) help you name what you see.
A hundred seeds weigh about 6.6 grams, so the higher this number, the bigger the seed. The seed coat is glossy green. The seed holds 21.63 percent crude protein.
What its seller and farm sources say

items: **Yield:** 1.38 t/ha dry season, 1.3 t/ha wet season.
**Fruit:** Glossy green seed, about 6.5 g per 100 seeds, crude protein about 21.6 percent, high stickiness.
**Where:** All regions, wet and dry seasons.
Resistant to Cercospora leaf spot and rust.

blocks.text: Why farmers know it: first of BPI's Luntian munggo series, approved after nearly seven years of testing and recommended for all regions. Check these against what farmers near you have seen, because the same variety can do differently from one town to the next.
Where and when to plant Luntian 1 mungbean

It is recommended for anywhere in the country in both the wet and the dry season. Munggo is ready in about two months, so it fits the gap after rice. Pick a variety that ripens its pods together, which saves picking rounds, and one rated against cercospora leaf spot and powdery mildew.

items.q: Is NSIC Mg 19 the same as Luntian 1?
items.a: Yes. NSIC Mg 19 is another name for Luntian 1, registered as NSIC 2018 Mg 19. Seed sellers use both, so ask for either one.

items.q: How long does it take to harvest?
items.a: It takes about 60 days from sowing to harvest. Then the weather and your care decide the exact day.
The record shows 1.34 tonnes per hectare on average in the trials. Your own yield depends on the soil, water, fertilizer and pests on your farm.
It is recommended for anywhere in the country in both the wet and the dry season. Ask your municipal agriculturist how it has done in your town.

items.q: Where can I buy seed of Luntian 1?
items.a: Ask an accredited seed dealer in your province, the seller named on this page or your municipal agriculturist. Look for the certified seed tag or a sealed pack before you pay.
